verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev ships an official MCP server that lets AI assistants get task information and trigger task runs, so an external agent can invoke a user's workflows through generic MCP tools. However, the server is aimed at developer and coding-assistant use (searching docs, deploying, monitoring), and there is no evidence that individual workflows can be published as their own named, schema-typed MCP tools. Missing for 10: per-workflow MCP tool exposure with custom schemas, exposure of connected app actions, production agent-facing auth and hosting details, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can expose my workflows or connected app actions as MCP tools that an external agent can call

citations.quote: Get task information and trigger task runs
The Trigger.dev MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server enables AI assistants to interact directly with your Trigger.dev projects.
Give your AI assistant direct access to Trigger.dev tools — search docs, trigger tasks, deploy projects, and monitor runs.
